messages:
Maya: Quick Q — bringing up a new 13B-ish model on H100s across us-east / eu-west. We're seeing different kernel winners per region/seq profile. Rules of thumb for choosing FlashAttention v2 vs v3 vs Triton/vendor libs? Also safe rollout heuristics?

Siddharth: short answer: Flashv3 for long seqs and bursty single-request latency; vendor/Triton kernels for short seqs and heavy packing. Longer version below.

Ben: ran a small benchmark (13B, q8) in us-east H100s earlier:
- flashv2: p50=28ms p99=210ms throughput=420 tok/s (seq=64 batch=1)
- flashv3: p50=22ms p99=190ms throughput=510 tok/s (seq=64 batch=1)
- triton-vendor: p50=20ms p99=350ms throughput=600 tok/s (seq=64 batch=8)
Region eu-west was ~10-12% higher p99 across configs.

Maya: that p99 hit on Triton vendor is pretty bad for tail-heavy services.

Siddharth: vendor kernels like Triton-optimized or NVIDIA FT push packing/throughput hard. They win when you can pack many requests (batch>4) and seq<128. Flashv3 introduced kernel fusion and optimized attention for H100 memory layout which reduces tail for longer seqs; v2 is okay but slower on high concurrency long sequences.

Olga: also remember quant mode affects this a lot. We saw quality flicker with Q4_0 on some instruction prompts; Q8 was safer quality-wise but changes perf shape. Test quality alongside perf.

perf-bot: ran nightly-bench/13b-q8 on h100-us-east at 2134567000
```
seq=64 batch=1: flashv2 p50=30ms p99=220ms
seq=64 batch=8: triton-vendor p50=20ms p99=360ms
seq=512 batch=1: flashv3 p50=110ms p99=260ms
```

Ben: rollout heuristic we've used: 1) Canary flashv3 at 5% per-region with route-matching; 2) Monitor p50/p99, error rate, and quality evals for 10m windows; 3) If p99 > baseline by 25% or error rate >0.5% rollback; 4) Circuit-breaker to fallback to flashv2 or vendor kernel based on request shape.

Maya: how do you detect request shape reliably in prod?

Siddharth: sample request headers and maintain a rolling 5m histogram of sequence lengths and batch sizes. Heuristic: if median_seq < 128 and 90th < 256 => prefer vendor kernel; else prefer flashv3. Apply per-route config so chat endpoints with short history use vendor packer, long-context evaluation routes use flashv3.

Olga: watch microburst/warmup effects — vendor kernels benefit from sustained packing. Flashv3 tends to win for bursty single-request traffic because of lower tail. Also keep an eye on kernel swap frequency: too many flips cause cache churn.

Maya: got it. Any specific metrics to export to the console?

Ben: export: token-level latency (p50/p95/p99), kernel-selection-counts, packing-efficiency (% requests packed), KV-cache hit rate, and quality-safeguard failures. Also track kernel-switches-per-minute and add hysteresis (30s min before allowing another switch).

Siddharth: add a lightweight in-prod eval: sample 10 eval prompts every 5m, compute logprob delta vs baseline; if delta > threshold don't promote. This catches subtle quant/quality regressions that perf numbers won't show.

Maya: perfect — I'll codify this into the runbook and schedule a canary for tomorrow. Will coordinate with infra for capacity and with infra/regions for fallback images.

Olga: :thumbsup:
